journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
directions: Out of the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side, north past the farm with its cattle and its big house, to the bank of the channel beyond.

journal_text: Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
directions: The estate house is the big house on the farm north of the town, by the cattle; Hulm-Tei stands inside it. Brings-Them-Back stands where the channel runs on north of the bank.

journal_text: I took Rows-For-Another's leaf from the count-box and left Never-Sold's in its place. Under it lay the keeper's own leaf, with Hulm-Tei's name on it: whatever any leaf comes up short is written onto his. If I hand hers in, her eleven years fall on him. I'm to bring hers to Never-Sold, or give Hulm-Tei back his own.
directions: Back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side.

journal_text: I talked Brings-Them-Back round. He will look the other way when Rows-For-Another goes by the channel, but he still knows the way to her home tree. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
directions: Rows-For-Another stands on the channel bank north of the farm.

journal_text: I paid Brings-Them-Back 150 gold, his head-price. He will look the other way when Rows-For-Another goes by the channel, but he still knows the way to her home tree. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
directions: Rows-For-Another stands on the channel bank north of the farm.

journal_text: I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
directions: Rows-For-Another stands on the channel bank north of the farm.

journal_text: I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
directions: Back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side.

journal_text: I talked Hulm-Tei round. He took the first price, struck Rows-For-Another's leaf and wrote her eleven years onto his own, knowing what he did. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side.

journal_text: I gave Hulm-Tei back his own leaf with the first price. He struck Rows-For-Another's leaf and said the damp had taken his. He leaves the estate at the reckoning, and what she owed will be shared among the hands who stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side.

journal_text: I paid Hulm-Tei the whole of what Rows-For-Another's leaf had grown to, 1,000 gold. He struck her leaf, and nobody carries anything for it. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side.

journal_text: I gave Never-Sold Rows-For-Another's leaf, and she will read it aloud and burn it. Rows-For-Another is free; her eleven years fall on Hulm-Tei's leaf, or on every hand of the estate if his leaf is gone too. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Hulm-Tei struck Rows-For-Another's leaf with his own hand. She is free, and what it cost fell where his word put it. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Her Owing was never closed: it will be written onto the keeper, and the fetcher still knows the way to her home tree, so she can never go back to it. Never-Sold paid me half, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.

I gave Never-Sold Rows-For-Another's leaf, which I had taken from the estate's count-box before she asked me. She will read it aloud and burn it, and the eleven years fall on the estate's keeper. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.
Never-Sold or Rows-For-Another is dead. The Owing cannot be ended now.

Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore, where the heirs of the Rose keep three of their held. One of the three can be got out. She wants the one held for words, not the one held for a killing. I'm to speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, who keeps the post.
directions: Out of the Chainbreakers' house and south through the town to the east shore, where the heirs' post stands; Tsaxi stands on the water by the nearest houses.

journal_text: Tsaxi can count one of the three lost to the Rose's fire, and no more. Walks-Far and Mends-Nets each claim to be held for words; one killed a man. The leaves that say which are with the Rose's reckoner, lost in the western swamp. I'm to learn who is who, and read the leaves if I find them.
directions: The reckoner's camp is the hut in the swamp far west of the town, round the lake by the wet road.

journal_text: I took the singed leaves from the reckoner's strongbox in the western swamp and read them. Walks-Far is held for words; Mends-Nets drowned Reckoner Otheel and is to be put under, sent down below the Rose where the dead walk; Seven-Floods owes for a roof. Before I choose who goes, I'm to tell Seven-Floods what I read.
directions: Back east round the lake to the heirs' post on the east shore.

journal_text: I told Seven-Floods what the leaves say. Mends-Nets drowned Otheel for her, after Otheel wrote a third winter on her roof, and Seven-Floods asks me to take Mends-Nets out anyway, before her. Now I'm to choose who goes.
directions: The three stand east of Tsaxi, on the water's edge.

journal_text: I talked Tsaxi round. He will count one of the three lost to the smoke. I'm to tell the one I choose to go.
directions: The three stand east of Tsaxi, on the water's edge.

journal_text: I paid Tsaxi 300 gold. He will count one of the three lost to the smoke. I'm to tell the one I choose to go.
directions: The three stand east of Tsaxi, on the water's edge.

journal_text: I gave Tsaxi the reckoner's leaves and told him his hut was empty but for a lamia. He kept them. The count is his now, and he will say one died of the smoke. I'm to tell the one I choose to go.
directions: The three stand east of Tsaxi, on the water's edge.

journal_text: I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
directions: The three stand east of Tsaxi, on the water's edge.

journal_text: I told Walks-Far to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back through the town to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back through the town to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I told Seven-Floods to go when I had gone. She will go to her daughter first. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
directions: Back through the town to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I told all three to go. I'm to tell Never-Sold the post is empty.
directions: Back through the town to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I told Never-Sold that Walks-Far came out. Mends-Nets stays, to be put under if her leaf is ever read, and Seven-Floods stays far from her Hist. Never-Sold was pleased and uneasy, paid me 150 gold and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out. Walks-Far stays to work his three seasons, and Seven-Floods stays far from her Hist. Never-Sold said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Seven-Floods came out, to go to her daughter. Walks-Far stays to work his three seasons, and Mends-Nets stays, to be put under if her leaf is ever read. Never-Sold was silent a while, then kind, paid me 150 gold and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold the post is empty. She paid me nothing: the Rose's hunters, short three, will take a clutch-brother of Walks-Far's in their place, and the heirs will not treat with the Chainbreakers again. She said to come back to her for more work all the same.
Never-Sold is dead. Nobody will take word of who came out of the post.

Never-Sold sent me to Soulrest's dock. The Broker, Ussa-Rekh, bought a crew free and keeps a carved token for each until they work a season for him; he has kept them a season more. Never-Sold wants the tokens, and the book on the Broker's shelf with Never-Sold on its spine. I'm to speak to Heavy-Rope by the docks.
directions: Soulrest's dock lies on the shore a short way east of Lilmoth, where the map says Docks.

journal_text: Heavy-Rope told me the tokens are in the Broker's chest, in the north one of the three houses by the dock. The old man keeps the key on him, and Feldril Nethri keeps about outside the locked door. The berth-master Ra'Jhan pays for the season when it is sailed. I'm to free the crew by one of the three.
directions: The Broker's house is the north house of Soulrest, up from the shore by the docks; Ussa-Rekh is usually inside it and Feldril Nethri keeps about outside its locked door. Ra'Jhan stands on the bare shore where the dock meets the land.

journal_text: I talked Feldril Nethri round. He unbarred the Broker's door for me. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
directions: The Broker's house is the north house of Soulrest; its door now stands unbarred.

journal_text: I paid Feldril Nethri 30 gold. He unbarred the Broker's door for me. I'm to free the crew by the chest, the Broker or the berth-master.
directions: The Broker's house is the north house of Soulrest; its door now stands unbarred.

journal_text: I took the crew's tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest. His room was lit and cluttered, a chest, a shelf and three beds, and a book with Never-Sold's name on its spine stood on the shelf. He keeps the eleven names at Thorn on his table, a price beside each. I'm to bring the tokens to Heavy-Rope.
directions: Back down from the north house to the shore by the docks.

journal_text: I talked Ra'Jhan into giving up the season. The hire is void. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope.
directions: Heavy-Rope stands on the shore by the docks.

journal_text: I paid Ra'Jhan 1,000 gold to give up the season. The hire is void. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope.
directions: Heavy-Rope stands on the shore by the docks.

journal_text: Ra'Jhan is dead. With the berth-master dead, the hire is void. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope.
directions: Heavy-Rope stands on the shore by the docks.

journal_text: I talked Ussa-Rekh round. He let the crew go and will sign his own season to the berth-master. He gave me his key, for the tokens are in his chest. I'm to bring them to Heavy-Rope.
directions: The chest stands in his room; Heavy-Rope on the shore by the docks.

journal_text: I paid Ussa-Rekh the season's hire, 1,000 gold, out of my own purse. He let the crew go. He gave me his key, for the tokens are in his chest. I'm to bring them to Heavy-Rope.
directions: The chest stands in his room; Heavy-Rope on the shore by the docks.

journal_text: The crew are free of the last season. Heavy-Rope gave me 150 gold of the crew's thanks. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended, and bring her the book from the Broker's shelf with her name on its spine.
directions: East along the coast and south through the marsh to Blackrose, to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I gave Heavy-Rope the crew's tokens and told him the Broker let them go. He gave me 150 gold of the crew's thanks. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended, and bring her the book from the Broker's shelf with her name on its spine.
directions: East along the coast and south through the marsh to Blackrose, to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: Heavy-Rope will sail the last season, for the eleven at Thorn. He chose it himself, and bitterly. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended, and bring her the book from the Broker's shelf with her name on its spine.
directions: East along the coast and south through the marsh to Blackrose, to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: Feldril Nethri took the bar off the Broker's door: with the crew's matter settled, he said, it is no longer his to keep. I'm to bring Never-Sold the book from the Broker's shelf with her name on its spine, and tell her how it ended at the dock.
directions: The Broker's house is the north house of Soulrest, up from the shore by the docks; the book stands on the shelf in his room. Then east along the coast and south through the marsh to Blackrose, to the Chainbreakers' house on its north side.

journal_text: I told Never-Sold what the Broker's house held: a shack, eleven names at Thorn on his table that his hire was to buy free, and her own name in his book as the keeper of the count at Tulm-Varo. She took the book and answered once, plainly. I'm to tell her how it ended at the dock.
directions: Never-Sold stands in the Chainbreakers' house.

journal_text: I told Never-Sold the crew are free of the season. The eleven at Thorn have lost the hire that was to buy them out. She gave me lockpicks, named me a full Chainbreaker and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Ussa-Rekh let the crew go himself, and that somebody paid for it, the old man or my own purse. She went quiet, then said, "He would. That is the worst of him." She gave me lockpicks, named me a full Chainbreaker and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Heavy-Rope will sail the last season for the eleven at Thorn. The crew lose the ending they were promised. She named me a full Chainbreaker and gave me nothing else: "Eleven. I cannot tell you that you were wrong. I can tell you he will ask again." She said to come back to her for more work.
Never-Sold or Heavy-Rope is dead. The crew have nobody to speak for them now.

I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof comes into sight about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me his people began charging walkers at the ford. The landing folk worked this ford before the well was dug. They will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing folk will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and showed Signs-For-The-Cargo the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing folk would take half a charge for water they never draw. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it.
directions: Livia Varinius keeps the well inside the station walls; Signs-For-The-Cargo stands at the raft on the landing stage across the ford.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing folk will ram their clay in behind the cracked lining. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing folk will make no terms with Livia Varinius while they mourn. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to search the pool, with her leave or without it.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I found a dead man staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring and took the rope that tied his wrists. The stake through him is blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal keeps to the lodge.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro will raise the body and give it to the Hist, and Reeh-Shaal is to be held for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro will raise the courier's body from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her be. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The villagers have closed ranks against me.

At Helstrom's landing, Okan-Zish of the landing crew told me a crocodile lairs in the shallows east of the scaffold. It took one of their rafts, and no raft has gone out since. I'm to kill it; it lies east of the rock roots where he stands, a short walk through the shallows.
directions: Okan-Zish stands on the rock roots at the landing. The crocodile lies in the shallows east of the scaffold, a short walk east of him.

journal_text: The crocodile in the shallows by the scaffold at Helstrom's landing is dead. I'm to tell Okan-Zish, the rafter of the landing crew who wanted it gone; he stands on the rock roots at the landing.
directions: Okan-Zish stands on the rock roots at the landing.

journal_text: Okan-Zish admitted the beast was the crew's doing: Wuleen-Taza dumped offal in the shallows east of the scaffold to scare traders off Sells-Dear's boat, and it drew a real crocodile. The crew left their bait bucket there. I'm to fetch it for Sells-Dear, the boat captain, which costs the crew their trade, or take Wuleen-Taza's price to keep quiet.
directions: The bucket lies in the shallows east of the scaffold. Wuleen-Taza stands east of Okan-Zish, near the bridge. Sells-Dear stands far north of the landing crew, on bare ground by the houses, with tents a short walk east of her.

journal_text: I have the crew's bait bucket, still sour with offal. I'm to show it to Sells-Dear, the boat captain, far north of the crew, on bare ground by the houses, and the crew lose their trade; or take Wuleen-Taza's price near the bridge and keep quiet.
directions: Sells-Dear stands far north of the landing crew, on bare ground by the houses; Wuleen-Taza east of Okan-Zish, near the bridge.

journal_text: I showed Sells-Dear, the boat captain, the crew's bait bucket. She kept it and paid me 60 gold, and with the rafters' trick known the river trade is hers. The landing crew have lost it: no trader hires their rafts now, and Okan-Zish and Wuleen-Taza have no work at the landing.

Wuleen-Taza paid me 60 gold to say nothing of the bait. The crew keep their trade, but I took coin to hide a trick that drew a real beast to the shallows by their scaffold, and Sells-Dear, the boat captain, still thinks the crocodile came up the river on its own.
Okan-Zish, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. What the crew asked of me ends with him.
Sells-Dear, the boat captain of Helstrom, is dead. What was asked of me at the landing ends with her.
Wuleen-Taza, a rafter of Helstrom's landing crew, is dead. What was asked of me at the landing ends with her.

Haj-Wan, by the paved road at Helstrom, told me her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to the Agaceph and has not come back. Their custom forbids his own to follow, but not an outsider. I'm to find him out among the trees, a long way east past the houses.
directions: East from the road, a long way past the houses; Sei-Wan is on dry ground among the trees there.

journal_text: I found Sei-Wan on dry ground out among the trees, a long way east of Helstrom's road. A viper lies south-west of him, a short walk off, and he will not come home while it lives. I'm to kill the viper.
directions: The viper lies among the trees south-west of Sei-Wan, a short walk off.

journal_text: The viper among the trees is dead, and Sei-Wan can walk home. Haj-Wan wants him home alive; he wants the walk-out to be his own. I'm to speak to him and choose: talk him home, which costs him the walk-out, or tell him to walk home alone and say nothing at the road.
directions: Sei-Wan is on dry ground a long way east of Haj-Wan, past the houses.

journal_text: Sei-Wan gave in and said he will come home, though not at my heels, and he will not count the walk-out as his own. Haj-Wan has waited for him since he left. I'm to tell her by the paved road, back west past the houses, near Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden.
directions: Haj-Wan waits by the paved road near the levy warden, back west past the houses.

journal_text: I told Sei-Wan to walk home on his own feet and left him on dry ground out in the basin, and I said nothing of it to Haj-Wan. His walk-out stays his own. Haj-Wan keeps waiting by the road and knows nothing.

I told Haj-Wan by the road that Sei-Wan is coming home, and she paid me 60 gold. She is glad he lives, and sorry that he lost the walk-out he went into the basin to win. I talked him out of it, and he will not thank me.
Sei-Wan, a young Agaceph of Helstrom, is dead in the basin. Whatever Haj-Wan asked of me for him ends with him, and the walk-out is lost to him for good.
Haj-Wan, who waited by Helstrom's road for her kin Sei-Wan, is dead. Whatever she wanted of me ends with her.
